newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ long bond yields close near 8.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: NZ long bond yields close near 8.0 percent.

text.p: 0500 GMT
* NZ 10 year bonds approach 8.0 percent
* TransAlta bond rate set encourages further buying
* GDP data mildly encouraging
* Cash at 10.0 pct vs 9.95 pct at Thursday's close
* TWI at 66.60 from 66.79
* 90 day bills 9.94 pct vs 9.91 pct
* 7/98 bond yields 8.05 pct vs 8.08 pct
* 02/01 bond yields 8.07 pct vs 8.15 pct
* 11/06 bond yields 8.03 pct vs 8.10 pct
* Dec bank bill futures 90.60 vs 90.61, vol 1942
Dealers said a rate set of NZ$111 million of Transalta bonds at 8.86 percent helped spur fresh buying. They said it appeared there was more hedging to be done on the transaction.
GDP data showing the economy grew 0.3 percent in the June quarter against average expectations of 0.4 percent was also mildly positive, although the data is well out of date.
However, bank bills took little comfort from the data, with the 90-days up three pips at 9.94 percent.
Despite increasing signs the left-of-centre parties are performing well in polls and in the election campaign, financial markets continue to take little note.
New Zealand long bonds ended another positive day on Friday with the 10-year bonds nearing the psychological 8.0 percent level.
Yields fell another seven basis points to finish off a strong week.
Local dealers suggest that with an election only 15 days away yields are approaching the bottom of their range but offshore buying shows no sign of abating.
Dealers said if the 10-years were pushed below resistance at 8.0 percent any breakthrough could see them quickly jump down to 7.75 percent.
-- Simon Louisson 64 4 4734 746
